questions.q: According to Zinsser, what is the key to clear writing?
a: Ruthlessly cut unnecessary words and phrases
Use as many fancy words as possible
Write long sentences to show depth
Cover several ideas in each paragraph
questions.why: Lesson 1 says complex writing is bad writing and urges you to delete anything that does not serve the message.

questions.q: Why does the summary advise spending extra time on beginnings?
a: Readers who dislike the intro will not keep reading
Editors judge submissions mostly by the opening line
Beginnings are easier to write than endings
A strong opening removes the need for a conclusion
questions.why: Lesson 2 warns that a terrible introduction stops readers no matter how good the rest is.

questions.q: What does the summary compare a paragraph ending to?
a: The cliffhanger at the end of a TV episode
The closing credits of a film
The headline of a news article
The summary at the end of a report
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares a strong paragraph ending to the hook at the end of a TV episode.

questions.q: What should a conclusion avoid doing, according to the summary?
a: Summarizing the whole piece in detail
Recapping the benefits in a line or two
Reminding readers what they gained
Ending on a quick, clean note
questions.why: Lesson 2 advises a brief review and recap of benefits rather than a long summary.

questions.q: How does the summary say you can inspire readers?
a: Write about subjects that genuinely interest you
Follow the prompts you were given in school
Write for the widest possible audience
Stick to topics that are proven to sell
questions.why: Lesson 3 says passion for your subject shines through and makes readers connect with your work.
